newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia lists bidders to build and run power plant.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia lists bidders to build and run power plant.

text.p: Tunisia on Thursday said it had shortlisted ten firms based in Britain, France, the United States, Switzerland and Belgium in a tender process to build and run a 350-to-500 megawatts power plant.

The shortlist, obtained by Reuters, is as follows: ABB Energy Ventures (Switzerland), British Gas (Great Britain), Comunity Energy Alternatives (United States), Destec Energy Europe (France), Electricite de France (EDF, France) and Enron Development Corp. (Great Britain).
Also included on the list are Intergen (Great Britain), National Power International (Great Britain), Entergy Power Development Corp. (Great Britain) and Powerfin (Belgium).
Western diplomatic sources said some firms associated to other power plant builders, such as U.S.' Bechtel, were not named.

The tender for final qualification is "imminent," officials said. More than 50 firms had shown interest in the concession when they attended a presentation of the project called Independent Power Production IPP in Tunis last April.
IPP is for the development of a combined-cycle gas turbine station, which could supply 350-to-500 megawatts of electricty by the start of the next century.

The qualified firm will build and run the plant at Rades in southern Tunis. Electricity produced there is to be supplied to the state-owned Societe Tunisienne de l'Electricite et du Gaz STEG for distribution under a long term contract, energy sources said.

It will be the first power plant to be privately-run after the Tunisian parliament in March approved a law scratching the state monopoly on power generation and allowing private investors to run power plants.
STEG will keep its existing production plants and distribution of electricity.
Officials said the country needs to build one 300 megawatts plant each two years.
